title: QL-1.01 Red-team gate: no contract is signed without a clean record that matches its spec
request: Closes quality-loop principle 1 (red-team each contract before signing) and the signing-time part of principle 2 (red-green primary, document-only checks never count toward done). A zero-dependency node script reads a contract spec and its red-team record and reports SIGNABLE, NOT SIGNABLE with reasons, or NO RECORD; a test proves every refusal rule; the seed-gate and the sign runbook call it. Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: SR-0.03.

tasks.title: The gate script and its refusal rules
requirements: scripts/gate/redteam-gate.mjs takes spec paths (default: every file under contracts/seed-readiness/specs/ and contracts/quality-loop/specs/) and prints one line per spec: SIGNABLE, NOT SIGNABLE: <reasons>, or NO RECORD; exit 0 only when every named spec is SIGNABLE; --report mode exits 0 unless a record is malformed, a hash mismatch is claimed clean, or a signed contract under contracts/signed/ has a spec without a SIGNABLE record

the record is contracts/<area>/redteam/<id>.json with schema memev-redteam/1, each round of kind spec (the default) or implementation, and snapshots <id>.r<n>.spec.json beside it; spec_sha256 is sha256 of the spec as canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace, workdir null)

SIGNABLE requires all of: record parses with the schema and the spec id; rounds numbered 1..n without gaps; the last round has verdict clean and holds no answer of severity high (medium and low answers may remain, each with its disposition), or the record ends with a valid stop decision; its spec_sha256 equals the spec on disk; every answer in every round has disposition added or rejected; every added answer's criterion, or its folded_as when the builder records one (the criterion the answer became, as task, statement and verifier), is present verbatim in the spec on disk, and a folded_as never names a criterion already verbatim in that round's own snapshot; every rejected answer has a non-empty reason; the sequence of snapshots never weakens (no task or criterion removed, no requirement reworded, no criterion statement or verifier key changed, no metric loosened, no scope glob added or broadened) except as requirement 6 accepts; every implement task has at least one test_red_green criterion unless the spec's manifest row declares kind docs or evidence; every input file of the clean round whose blob at HEAD differs is reported, and under src/ it is NOT SIGNABLE
node 23 compatible, no dependencies, first lines carry // gate-version: 1 and the SPDX header

each round is a DSSE envelope signed by a reviewer key that is not a contract-signing key (not under contracts/keys/); the gate holds the reviewer public keys it accepts and refuses an unsigned round, a round signed by another key, and any edit to an earlier round, snapshot or disposition after a later round was signed. Honest limit, stated in docs/CONTRACTS.md: while the builder and reviewer run as one user on one machine the reviewer key is readable by both, so the signature makes tampering visible in history but is not separation; separation comes from a reviewer key the owner holds off the build machine or from the second human of SR-9.05

a change between snapshots to a requirement's text, a criterion's statement or any key of a criterion's verifier is accepted only when the round's amendments list records it as {task, field, from, to, answer}, where answer is a citation as requirement 11 allows of an answer or note that the change carries out, and the next round judges whether it weakens; a glob added to a scope is accepted only when the amendments list cites an added answer of the previous round whose criterion reads a path under the glob, and otherwise the added paths are listed one by one; a criterion, requirement or stop rule removed is accepted only when the amendments list records it as {task, field, from, to: null, answer} whose citation names the removed text contradictory or impossible, or when a move entry carries it to a spec where it is verbatim, and the next round judges whether it weakens; the never-weakens check accepts exactly these and nothing else
staleness is judged at the signing commit for a contract already signed, and at HEAD for a spec not yet signed, so a signed contract's own landed work never makes it stale

the check is engine code that ships with memev: src/engine/redteam-gate.mjs exports evaluate({spec, cwd, reviewerKeys}), RULES, REVIEWER_KEYS and GRANDFATHERED, and scripts/gate/redteam-gate.mjs is a thin command-line wrapper over it, so the copies other repositories receive and the engine's own draft and sign paths run the same code

the committed base fixture is signed once with the real reviewer key, whose private key is never committed; every other fixture is signed with the test key under test/fixtures/redteam/ and reaches the gate only through an injected reviewerKeys argument

a round's signature covers its answers and its spec snapshot; that round's dispositions and amendments, written after the reviewer answered, are covered by the next round's signature, and the last round's own dispositions and amendments are covered by a closing envelope that a reviewer key signs over canonical({spec id, last round number, its dispositions and amendments}), or, at the stop, by the stop decision

a citation in an amendments list is one of: an answer of the previous round, as answer '<round>.<n>'; a numbered point of that round's notes, as note '<round>.<point>'; an answer of an implementation round recorded after the previous spec round, as answer '<round>.<n>'; an answer of another spec's record, as answer '<spec>:<round>.<n>', the spec id resolved through the manifest to a record under contracts/, never through a path; or an entry of the record's reviewer_notes list, as reviewer_note <n>, where each entry is {n, text, sig} and sig is a DSSE envelope by a key in REVIEWER_KEYS over {spec_id, n, text}; so every citation rests on a reviewer key's signature

a record may end with a stop decision only after three rounds of which none is clean: a DSSE envelope signed by a contract-signing key under contracts/keys/ over canonical({spec id, spec_sha256 of the spec on disk, decider, date, decision: sign or split, open: every answer of every round whose disposition is not added, as round and number, dispositions: the sha256 of canonical(every round's dispositions and amendments)}); the gate then prints SIGNABLE AT STOP (<n> open items) and --report lists the open items; a stop decision after fewer than three rounds, signed by any other key, over another spec hash, or whose open list leaves out an answer that is not added, is refused with stop_decision; the stop decision may carry an amendments list, which its signature covers, and the change from the last spec round's snapshot to the spec on disk is judged under requirement 6 with that list, its citations naming the last spec round as the previous round

RULES holds last_high (an answer of severity high in the last round) in place of the empty-round code, and adds stop_decision; docs/CONTRACTS.md states the stopping rule (clean: no high answer, every answer dispositioned), the stop decision and the implementation round of task T2

a round of kind implementation follows every rule a spec round follows (numbered after the rounds before it, signed by a reviewer key, every answer dispositioned, clean only when it holds no high answer, dispositions covered by a closing envelope) and names its reviewed commit; it judges the code at that commit against the signed contract and never changes whether the spec is SIGNABLE

an answer of a task that moved to another spec at a split is judged against the receiving spec: the round's amendments list records the move as {kind: move, task, to_spec, to_task, answer}; the answer's folded_as then names {spec, task, statement, verifier}; the gate resolves the spec id through the manifest to a spec under contracts/, never through a path the record gives, requires the criterion verbatim there at gating time, and follows the From/To chain of that spec's amendments across the move

every round's signature is verified when judging SIGNABLE, rounds after the last spec round included, and a round whose kind, or whose reviewer part (the round without sig, closing and the builder's fields disposition, reason, folded_as, amendments and folded), differs from the version that first committed it is refused with review_sig

--report judges a signed contract against the commit that added the round its record's verdict rests on now (the clean round the record ends with, or its stop decision), never an older commit whose version of the record held a clean round on the same hash

--report lists a signed contract that a later signed contract supersedes (version N+1 whose supersedes names it) as superseded; only the last version of each chain must equal the spec's drafted tasks and the hash its record makes signable

a stop decision is accepted only when its key's .pub under contracts/keys/ is committed at the commit being judged (HEAD for a spec not yet signed, the signing commit for one that is signed); a key present only in the working tree never signs a stop
